headline: Alphabet's record one-day loss, Amazon/Intel earnings and Marvell's $80bn Lumentum bid hit AI spenders and acquirers (Nasdaq -1.4%), while suppliers with orders (Vertiv, Quanta, GE Vernova, Sandisk) keep reporting demand.
regime: Nasdaq fell 1.4% and is heading for its first monthly loss since July, with the semis ETF -1.1% on the day but +7.3% on five days and -7.8% on the month. The 10-year is 4.99% and crude $104.37 (+15.4% on the month), so the discount rate and an oil shock still cap multiples. Weak Big Tech prints, rising AI financing costs and Intel's PC warning punished the buyers (hyperscalers -3.7%, software -7.3%, neoclouds -4.1%), while order-book names (power and grid +0.7% on the day, cooling +25.7% for Vertiv on five days) held up. Money is moving from AI spenders to AI suppliers with backlog, not out of the theme.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Vertiv Q3 sales +61% and organic orders more than doubled (304bae0ddaa9)
GE Vernova: gas turbine prices up 50%, buyers reserving slots years out, $197B backlog, $9B Trench deal (d06bf75b752f, 8d7ea789c245)
Quanta record $63.7B backlog (c7926fa7cd44); Trane raised revenue guidance (0765dff5592e)
Against: grid and power stocks still fall on beats (Hubbell, GEV -24% from high) (85d443ed03a0, cb6e1a152f53)
theses.change_note: +2: Vertiv's doubled orders and turbine slot reservations are the strongest bottleneck evidence yet; the market still pays unevenly, so the gain stays small.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Sandisk says it is sold out for the rest of the decade, raised outlook, 8-for-1 split (80b65c311518, d0e7f4dcbc9e)
Broadcom's $63B Anthropic financing gives it a funded customer (8bcade90d848)
Against: Intel flags prolonged PC weakness, HP and Dell -7% (9d7b5fffbf53)
Against: Google Cloud revenue more than doubled but the stock still fell on cash burn (4c6f3efd640e)
theses.change_note: Sandisk and Broadcom confirm supply tightness; Intel's PC warning is consumer, not data centre, so the two offset.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Cipher Digital -38% since $850M zero-coupon convertible sale, report Nov 2 must show the capex math (c46a585c93c9)
Nadella described a business model 'that is no business at all'; Oracle and CoreWeave dropped (bd96fc806ae5)
Segment -4.1% on the day and -19.9% on the month; 15 names failed the cash-flow gate today (digest segments, shortlist)
theses.change_note: +3: Cipher's convertible-funded slide and Nadella's remark add to financing stress; the quality gate again drops every neocloud.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Sandisk sold out through the decade yet the stock sold off hard (80b65c311518)
Segment +8.8% on five days but -18.2% on the month (digest segments)
Intel and Sandisk give opposite views of memory demand (225ef04bb559)
Against: Apple warned memory costs may squeeze margins (aee38c123837)
theses.change_note: +2: the shortage call got its strongest confirmation yet and the group trades 18% below a month ago, but selling on good news shows the market doubts durability.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Alphabet burned $9B in a quarter and set a record single-day loss (3aba6a8be1e2, 9455ea5fd8c8)
Amazon fell on earnings with Intel; Nasdaq futures -2% (4da78539866c)
Hyperscalers -3.7% on the day, -5.6% on the month; GOOGL -12.5% on five days (digest segments)
Against: Oracle +11.2% on five days despite the Nadella dig (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +2: Amazon joins Alphabet in disappointing, so the spenders' penalty is now broad rather than one name.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: 10-year 4.99%, crude $104.37 (+15.4% on the month), VIX +7.4% (digest tape)
Nasdaq-100 on track for first monthly loss since July on 'rising AI financing costs' (bff533a63390)
Software -7.3% on the day, ServiceNow -30% on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: +2: first monthly Nasdaq loss since July with oil above $100; the 10-year dipped under 5% so the rate leg did not worsen.

compute.note: -4.2% on the day, -10.8% on the month; Marvell -13% on its Lumentum bid shows the market punishing big spending.

foundry_equipment.note: -17.4% on the month but +7.7% on five days; quality names (TSM, ASML) are the only way in.

memory_storage.note: Sandisk sold out through the decade; group -18.2% on the month leaves a price cushion.

networking_optical.note: Lumentum +22% on five days is a takeover bid; fundamentals unchanged.

servers.note: Dell and HP -7% on Intel's PC warning; SMCI reports Nov 3.

power_nuclear.note: +0.7% on the day with NuScale-Doosan and Constellation 20-year deals; own cash-flow producers only.

grid_electrical.note: Quanta $63.7B backlog and GEV $197B backlog; sold-on-beats keeps entry prices fair.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv orders doubled and +25.7% on five days; less margin of safety after the run.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Convertible-funded capex (Cipher -38%) and -19.9% on the month; fails the cash-flow gate.

hyperscalers.note: Alphabet burn and Amazon miss; Nasdaq's loss is concentrated here.

ai_software.note: -7.3% on the day on ServiceNow's -30% five-day slide; AI is a cost to them, not a tailwind.

risks: More hyperscaler capex cuts after Alphabet and Amazon would hit every supplier despite strong backlogs.
Oil above $100 and a 10-year near 5% extend multiple compression in crowded AI names.
Neocloud convertible financing stress could cancel or delay GPU, power and cooling orders.
Sell-the-news on good prints (Sandisk, Hubbell, GEV) means being right on fundamentals can still lose money.
Marvell paying up for Lumentum signals late-cycle deal-making and dilution risk.
watch: Apple (Nov 2) on memory costs, and Cipher Digital's Nov 2 capex math.
SMCI earnings Nov 3 and Eaton Nov 3 for servers and grid demand.
Whether Marvell-Lumentum is formally announced and how optics names react.
Whether Alphabet and Amazon dip-buyers appear or the selling spreads to suppliers.
